s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of headache and vision loss with sinus inflammation and orbital involvement
salient_findings: Vision loss in the right eye for 2 days
Opacification of all sinuses on the right with diffuse inflammation
Bony erosion of the medial orbital apex bone
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 70s
No history of chronic or allergic rhinosinusitis
Diagnosed with COVID-19 three weeks prior to presentation
Recovered from COVID-19 but developed worsening headache and vision loss
Right eye visual acuity limited to hand-motion detection
Severe pain on ocular motion
Sinus cultures positive for Streptococcus constellatus
Elevated Serum IgG4 level
Dense infiltrate of IgG-containing plasma cells with most being IgG4 positive

shortlist.label: IgG4-related disease
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated Serum IgG4 level and dense infiltrate of IgG-containing plasma cells with most being IgG4 positive

shortlist.label: IgG4-related Ophthalmic Disease
shortlist.why_kept: IgG4-related disease with orbital involvement and vision loss

shortlist.label: Orbital Apex Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Bony erosion of the medial orbital apex bone and extension of inflammation into the apex

shortlist.label: Invasive Aspergillosis
shortlist.why_kept: Opacification of all sinuses on the right with diffuse inflammation and positive sinus cultures

shortlist.label: Mucormycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Rhino-orbital-cerebral involvement with vision loss and severe pain on ocular motion

raw.rationale: Elevated Serum IgG4 level and dense infiltrate of IgG-containing plasma cells with most being IgG4 positive are key findings that support this diagnosis

rejected.label: IgG4-related Ophthalmic Disease
rejected.why: While the patient has vision loss, the findings are more systemic and involve multiple sinuses, suggesting a broader disease process

rejected.label: Orbital Apex Syndrome
rejected.why: This diagnosis is possible given the bony erosion of the medial orbital apex bone, but it does not explain the elevated IgG4 levels or the systemic nature of the findings

rejected.label: Invasive Aspergillosis
rejected.why: There is no mention of fungal elements in the pathology or laboratory findings, making this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Mucormycosis
rejected.why: Similar to Invasive Aspergillosis, there is no evidence of fungal infection, and the presence of IgG4-positive plasma cells points away from this diagnosis
